newsitem.title: USA: APS sees 745 MW N.M. coal unit back Thurs.
newsitem.headline: APS sees 745 MW N.M. coal unit back Thurs.

text.p: Arizona Public Service Co (APS) expects its 745 megawatt (MW) coal-fired unit at its power plant near Farmington, N.M., would resume full output early Thursday, the company said Wednesday.
"It's in the startup process now. It should be back at full service tomorrow morning," said company spokesman Bruce Richardson.
The unit, part of the Four Corners facility, was shut Aug 22 to repair a leaking boiler tube.
APS, a subsidiary of Pinnacle West Capital Corp, has a 15 percent share in Four Corners' units 4 and 5.
Edison International's Southern California Edison Co has a 48 percent interest in units 4 and 5, each of which have a generation capacity of 745 MW.
Four Corners units 1 and 2 have a generation capacity of 170 MW, while unit 3 has a capacity of 220 MW.
